dedupe_keys.name: glad global cropland extent and change 30 m 2000 2019 potapov et al university of maryland

description: A globally consistent 30 m time series of cropland extent from Landsat, in five four-year epochs from 2000 to 2019. The GLAD dataset page defines cropland as land used for annual and perennial herbaceous crops for food, forage (including hay) and biofuel, excluding woody perennial crops, permanent pasture and shifting cultivation, with fallows limited to four years. Landsat time series were turned into phenology metrics and classified with locally calibrated machine learning models trained on visually interpreted high resolution imagery, giving one layer per epoch named 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015 and 2019 (values 0 and 1). The data are downloadable as 8-bit LZW-compressed GeoTIFF quadrant mosaics in WGS84 at 0.00025 degrees, about 1.8 GB per north-east tile per epoch, and also as Google Earth Engine assets with a viewer app; the reference paper is Potapov and others (2021) in Nature Food. Coverage is global land. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0. For simulation it tracks where cropland has spread or shrunk, to update the farm exposure layer and the demand for rural roads and irrigation in hazard and adaptation models. Related catalogue records include the global hybrid herbaceous cropland map and the Hansen Global Forest Change from the same laboratory.
